thread:
maria: FYI: spotted an RBAC grant with no actor in the audit stream for role 'analytics_reader' applied to service:analytics-job. Compliance flagged it during sample review.
devin: which timestamp and resource? can you paste the raw event?
maria: event id f2c8b9, shows action=grant, target=service:analytics-job, role=analytics_reader, actor=null, recorded_at=2026-02-12T14:22:07Z. attached the json snippet in case it helps.
alex: that usually means the authoring system called the permission service with an identity tied to a long-lived machine token that didn't propagate metadata. could be our self-service sync or a CRON job.
june: checking rotation windows — we rotated KMS key key-prod-rbac-7 last night. any chance KMS client failed to sign metadata and defaulted to service principal?
maria: maybe. audit-bot: Automatched rule: event.actor==null -> alert created -> ticket AI-4872.
devin: can we query the audit store for grants to that service in the 24h window around the rotation? i'll run a quick splunk query.
devin: Splunk snippet I'm running: 
```
index=audit events action=grant target="service:analytics-job" earliest=-12h latest=+12h | sort _time | table _time event_id actor metadata
```
alex: also include source_agent and token_id fields — token rotation bugs show up there.
june: pulling KMS logs now: KMS key key-prod-rbac-7 rotation step=complete at 2026-02-12T14:05:12Z. No errors in KMS side but I see increased retries on the permission-service around 14:21Z.
maria: Splunk results: two grant events, first by admin@maria (expected manual rollout) at 14:18Z, second at 14:22Z actor=null. both set same role.
devin: ok that smells like a retry from the sync worker that hit a credentials refresh path which returned a null actor when the token store returned expired metadata.
alex: can someone grep the sync-worker logs? query: 
```
grep -E "grant.*analytics-job" /var/log/sync-worker/* | sed -n '1,200p'
```
june: found entries: sync-worker restarted at 14:20Z due to OOM. PID changed, and the env loader logged a token refresh failure: "metadata: absent actor field, falling back to kernel-service".
maria: OOM caused process restart -> token cache cold -> token fetch path returned a minimal service token without actor metadata -> permission-service logged grant with actor=null.
devin: mitigation? revert is trivial but need compliance record. Suggest we: 1) backfill audit event actor field to show responsible deploy (we can annotate via admin@maria); 2) patch sync-worker to retry token fetch with exponential backoff and fail closed; 3) add alert for grants with null actor.
alex: for backfill, we need an authoritative mapping. Ops bot, can you append a synthetic audit entry linking event f2c8b9 to deploy-id=deploy-2026-02-12-analytics-restart and actor=ops@infra?
ops-bot: request received. Creating audit patch ticket PATCH-983 and emitting synthetic audit entry with source=ops-backfill, note="backfilled by sec-eng after investigation".
maria: I'll draft a compliance memo noting timeline and corrective actions; can whoever owns the sync-worker prod change confirm the patch PR by EOD? @devin @alex
devin: PR created: github.com/redwood/sync-worker/pull/421 — adds fail-closed token fetch, better metrics, and OOM mitigation knobs.
ajune: small ask from compliance: include a query and SHA for the backfilled entry so auditors can trace it. ops-bot: PATCH-983 includes patched_event_sha=8b1f4c and splunk_query_ref=AI-4872-splunk-1.
alex: one more long-term: make permission-service reject writes with actor==null (400) and surface error to caller so we never accept mystery grants. filing infra ticket INF-2416.
maria: agreed. good triage. closing slack thread once backfill is in and PR merged. thanks all :thumbsup:
